title: SNL Season 52 Kicks Off Tonight with NBA Champ Jalen Brunson and KATSEYE
summary:
Saturday Night Live is back for its 52nd season tonight, September 26, 2026 — and the premiere is bringing some serious star power.

Hosting the season opener is Jalen Brunson, point guard for the New York Knicks. He's fresh off leading his team to an NBA championship earlier this year. It's a bit unusual for an athlete to host the premiere rather than a later episode, but since Brunson represents a big win for New York City — where SNL is filmed — it fits.

The musical guest is KATSEYE, a global girl group whose members come from the Philippines, South Korea, Switzerland, and the United States. However, as of August 2026, two members — Manon and Sophia — announced they're taking a hiatus to focus on their mental health. It's unclear if they'll return for the SNL performance.

There are cast changes, too. Chloe Fineman left over the summer, and Bowen Yang departed mid-season last year. Returning repertory players include Kenan Thompson, Colin Jost, Michael Che, Mikey Day, Sarah Sherman, and Marcello Hernández. Ashley Padilla and Jane Wickline have been promoted from featured players. New faces Saidah Belo-Osagie and Grace Reiter are making their debut.

SNL is famous for being produced in just one week — cast and crew write, rehearse, and perform each episode in a frantic sprint. "SNL is a miracle every time it happens," the article notes.

Next week, October 3, Dakota Johnson hosts with musical guest Turnstile, the Grammy-winning rock band. Johnson is hosting for the third time, promoting her new movie "Verity."

You can watch SNL live at 11:30 p.m. ET on NBC and Peacock. Sketches hit YouTube shortly after, and full episodes stream on Peacock the next day.
why_it_matters: A 50-year-old live show staying relevant depends on constantly mixing worlds — sports fame, global pop and a nearly complete cast turnover — and on streaming and YouTube deciding which sketches become part of the wider culture the next morning.

background_read: Saturday Night Live (SNL) is a late-night sketch comedy show that first aired on NBC in 1975 and is performed live from Studio 8H in Rockefeller Center in New York City. Its creator, Lorne Michaels, still runs it. Cast and writers build a whole show in about six days, which is why it is often called a live miracle.

The cast is split into "repertory players" (the main, long-serving performers) and "featured players" (newer members who appear less often). Kenan Thompson has been on the show since 2003, making him its longest-serving cast member, while Bowen Yang is known as one of the show's first Chinese-American cast members.

Athletes regularly host the show because it lets them reach audiences far beyond sports — American football and basketball stars have done it before. KATSEYE is a global girl group formed through an international audition project run by a Korean entertainment company and a US record label, with members from different countries. NBC and the streaming service Peacock are owned by the same media company, which is why the show appears on both.

perspectives.perspective: New York Knicks fans and the city's audience
perspectives.description: For them a championship-winning point guard hosting the premiere is a celebration of a New York success story in a New York show. It also gives basketball fans who never watch comedy a reason to tune in.

perspectives.perspective: Viewers worried about the cast shake-up and KATSEYE's line-up
perspectives.description: Losing Chloe Fineman and Bowen Yang in the same year removes two distinctive voices, and promoting newcomers always carries risk in a live show. KATSEYE fans face a different worry: two of the group's members are on hiatus for mental health, so the performance may not be the full group.

SNL has survived five decades of cast changes because its brand is bigger than any performer, and the 'one-week miracle' format keeps it in the news. Casting an athlete over a comedian for the premiere shows how much the show now depends on cross-audience attention.

October already brings Dakota Johnson and Turnstile, suggesting a season built around promotion cycles for movies and albums. The real test is whether the promoted and brand-new cast members become the breakout names the show needs for its next decade.
